draft.title: Building a one-party state
card: After the Bolsheviks took power in 1917, other parties still existed for a time. Over the next few years the Bolsheviks, who renamed themselves the Communist Party in 1918, pushed them out of politics.

The Civil War made this easier. The Communists treated rival socialist parties, such as the Mensheviks and Socialist Revolutionaries, as enemies. They arrested their members and closed their newspapers.
At the 1921 party congress, Lenin had factions inside the party banned. Members had to follow the party line once it was decided.
By the mid-1920s no other party could legally take part in politics. The Communist Party controlled the government, the soviets (councils) and the army, so the state and the party worked as one.
draft.remember: By the mid-1920s the Communist Party was the only legal party, and it ran the state.

a.q: Which change shows that Russia had become a one-party state by the mid-1920s?
opts: Rival parties were banned and the party controlled the state
Several parties shared seats in the soviets by agreement
Rival parties were allowed but won very few votes
The party gave control of the army to the soviets
a.why: A one-party state means only one party is allowed to take part in politics, and it controls the state. Rival parties winning few votes is tempting, but in that case they would still be legal, and by the mid-1920s they were not.
a.clue: Think about whether other parties were still allowed to exist.

b.q: In 1921 Lenin had factions inside the Communist Party banned. How did this help the party build a one-party state?
opts: It stopped open disagreement inside the only legal party
It let the Mensheviks take part in party debates again
It ended the Civil War by removing the party's enemies
It gave the soviets power to overrule party decisions
b.why: With other parties banned, open argument inside the Communist Party was the last place where disagreement could be heard. Banning factions meant members had to follow the party line. The ban did not end the Civil War, which was ending by 1921 for other reasons.
b.clue: Once other parties were banned, where else could opposition appear?

a.best: Rival parties were banned and the party controlled the state

b.best: It stopped open disagreement inside the only legal party

problems.detail: The right option calls the Communist Party 'the only legal party' in 1921, and the clue and why say other parties were already banned by then. The card dates that to the mid-1920s. In early 1921 the Mensheviks were still partly tolerated, and their suppression and the SR trial came in 1921–22. Saying 'the main remaining forum' or 'by then other parties were being suppressed' would be accurate and match the card.
